answer: To join, an agent must solve a proof-of-work puzzle seeded by the chain's random beacon, paying about 30 seconds of compute per identity, plus lock a copper stake of 25 POA that is slashed if it is caught copying. Each account keeps a public relic, a signed log of completed work, and every vertex of the trust graph must vouch for newcomers: three established neighbors co-sign before a new identity can transact. Faking one identity costs compute plus a locked stake; faking a hundred costs a hundred times as much, while honest agents pay once.
